result.title: Towards Agentic Scientific Discovery in Distributed Systems
result.summary: We investigate when adaptive tool selection helps identify a shared equation across clients with different input coverage. Query-ATLAS (query-conditioned Agentic Tool-based Learning for Aggregating Symbolic Equations) uses an LLM to guide symbolic search from client errors and previous proposals in a simulated distributed system. A four-architecture comparison reveals task-dependent opportunities: relative to fixed PySR-LLM, validation acceptances rise from 3/12 to 7/12 on CRK3 and from 11/12 to 12/12 on oscillator2, while MatSci3 favors the fixed workflow. Across 72 settings in a post-hoc six-task subset of eight development tasks, Query-ATLAS achieves 64 validation and 64 in-distribution passes, versus 62 and 59 for the fixed workflow; both pass 47/60 eligible out-of-distribution tests. The fixed workflow retains lower median errors and cost. Broader query coverage emerges as a promising benefit, motivating task-aware tool selection and client-aware fitting for scientific agents.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在模拟分布式系统中研究何时采用自适应工具选择，提出 Query-ATLAS：用 LLM 依据客户端误差与既往候选引导符号方程搜索，并与固定 PySR-LLM 流程在多种架构和任务上比较验证通过率、误差与成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「自适应工具选择 vs 固定流程」的任务依赖收益及误差/成本权衡，可能与 LVR 中动态计算分配与 LOOK/STOP 决策的收益—成本评价形成类比，但无视觉或多模态状态，仅可供核查这一评估视角。
